JUDGMENT

This petition is filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 25-12-2018 at about 9.55 p.m., the petitioner was riding the two-wheeler Suzuki Access bearing No. KA-02-JV- 8620 with utmost care and caution.

When he was near Karnataka Spirit World, CBI fly over under pass, service road, Bengaluru, all of a sudden the rider of two-wheeler Pulsar-150 motorcycle bearing No.KA-50-V-8640 came with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, without observing the traffic rules and regulations, came in wrong direction in one way and dashed to the two-wheeler of petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to M/s. V.
Care Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
Earlier to the accident, the petitioner was Proprietor of M/s. A.K. Enterprises and earning Rs.1,00,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The R. T. Nagar Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 15% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing No. KA-50-V-8640 and its validity as on the date of accident.

It has contended that, there is negligence on the part of the Ajaaj Ahmed vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89363345/
2 petitioner himself by not taking proper care and precaution to ride the motorcycle, as the rider of the offending vehicle was riding the same slowly, carefully by following all traffic rules and regulations.

sentences.text: It has contended that, the petitioner and rider of the offending vehicle were not holding valid and effective driving licence and the petitioner was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident.

It has further contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties to the petition, since the insured and insurer of the motorcycle Suzuki Access bearing No.
KA-02-JV-8620 are not made parties to the claim petition.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident alleged to have occurred on 25-12-2018, at about 9:55 p.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motorcycle, bearing registration No.
KA-50-V-8640?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3. What order or Award?
6.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked total 22 documents as Ex.P.1 to 22.
Further, he has got examined two more witnesses namely Ms. Asma Noor and Dr. S. A. Somashekara as P.W.2 and P.W.3 and closed his side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 22 documents as Ex.P.1 to 22.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of First Information Statement, Ex.P.2 is copy of F.I.R, Ex.P.3 is true copy of Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is true copy of Sketch, Ex.P.5 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.6 is true copy of Wound Certificate, Ex.P.7 is true copy of Charge- sheet, Ex.P.8 is true copy of notice under Sec.133 of M.V. Act, Ex.P.9 is true copy of reply to said notice, Ex.P.10 is true copy indemnity bond, Ex.P.11 is notarised copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.12 is notarised copy of PAN card, Ex.P.13 are medical bills (total 28), Ex.P.14 are medical prescriptions (total 2), Ex.P15 are x-rays (total 2) with reports, Ex.P.16 is copy of in-patient bill, Ex.P.17 is discharge summary, Ex.P.18 is copy of MLC extract, Ex.P.19 is copy of test reports, Ex.P.20 is copy of case-sheet, Ex.P.21 is x-ray and Ex.P.22 is OPD record.

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 10, prima-facia it reveals that, on 25-12- 2018 at about 9.55 p.m., when the petitioner was riding his two-wheeler Suzuki Access bearing No.KA-02-JV-8620 near Karnataka Spirit World, CBI fly over under pass,
service road, Bengaluru, all of a sudden the rider of motorcycle bearing No. KA-50-V-8640, came in high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the two-wheeler of petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

The investigation officer in his final report has clearly stated that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, due to rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-50-V-8640 the said accident took place and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of his body.

12. Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/respondent No.2, as the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and contest the case of petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.1 insurance company, though has specifically denied the said facts in its written statement, it has not produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Even the respondent No.1 insurance company has not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.
There is no evidence on record to show that, due to rash and negligent driving of the petitioner himself the said accident has caused.

Further, the petitioner/P.W.1, has unequivocally denied the suggestions made to him in his cross- examination that, it was dark at the time of accident and due to his own rash and negligent driving he himself has fell down from his motorcycle and sustained injuries and not due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending motorcycle bearing No. KA-50-V-8640.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 Ajaaj Ahmed vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89363345/
4 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

sentences.text: 13. The Ex.P.3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has occurred when the petitioner was taking right turn near Karnataka Spirit World, from CBI fly over under pass service road, Bengaluru and the offending motorcycle was proceeding in wrong direction on the said one way road.
The rider of offending motorcycle riding his motorcycle in wrong direction on a one way road itself proves his negligent driving.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.7,
that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-50-V-8640.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the petitioner has sustained injuries due to his self rash and negligent driving and there is no negligence on the part of rider of offending motorcycle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, negligence of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. The learned counsel for respondent No.1 vehemently argued that, as per Ex.P.5 Motor Vehicle Accident report, no damage has been caused to the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-50-V-8640,
whereas the front right side shape, front right side indicator and front right side all round guard of the motorcycle ridden by the petitioner bearing Reg. No. KA-02-JV-8620 are damaged.

This clearly goes to show that, the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-50-V-8640 was not at all involved in the alleged accident and the petitioner has sustained injuries on account of his self fall from the above motorcycle ridden by him.
The arguments advanced by the learned counsel for respondent No.1 does not hold good.

Because, there are every chances that, if the offending motorcycle dashes to an oncoming vehicle in high speed and if the said vehicle does not fall down, obviously no damage will be caused to said motorcycle.

15. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.17 discharge summary, Ex.P.20 case sheet, Ex.P.21 x-ray and Ex.P.22 OPD record, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered comminuted fracture of 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th metatarsal of left foot and medial cuneiform fracture 1st metatarsal bones with dislocation of left foot, contusion injury left knee and contusion injury right ring finger.
The same has been deposed by the P.W.3, who is doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability suffered by the petitioner due to injuries sustained in the accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.3 in length

,
nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has not led any evidence to substantiate the contentions taken in its written statement.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can Ajaaj Ahmed vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89363345/

No. KA-50-V-8640 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

entities.text:
Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

sentences.text: 18. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 25-12-2018 at about 9.55 a.m., near Karnataka Spirit World, CBI Fly Over Under Pass, Service Road, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-50-V-8640.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-50-V-8640 and he has sustained comminuted fracture of 2nd,
3rd, 4th and 5th metatarsal of left foot and medial cuneiform fracture 1st metatarsal bones with dislocation of left foot, contusion injury left knee and contusion injury right ring finger and for the said injuries he has underwent surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock,
loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.,

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the copy of his Aadhar card and PAN card, which is marked as Ex.P.11 and 12.
As per Ex.P.11 and 12, the date of birth of the petitioner is 05-02-1959.
The accident has taken place on 25-12-2018 at about 9:55 P.M.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 60 years.

sentences.text: Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor who has examined and treated the petitioner has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered comminuted fracture of 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th metatarsal of left foot and medial cuneiform fracture 1st metatarsal bones with dislocation of left foot, contusion injury left knee and contusion injury right ring finger.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has 26% physical disability of right lower limb and for the whole body he has 13% physical disability.
The oral evidence of P.W.3 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.6 wound certificate,
Ex.P.17 discharge summary, Ex.P.20 case sheet, Ex.P.21 x-ray and Ex.P.22 OPD record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered comminuted fracture of 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th metatarsal of left foot and medial cuneiform fracture 1 st metatarsal bones with dislocation of left foot, contusion injury left knee and contusion injury right ring finger.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, no disability as assessed by him has been suffered by the petitioner due to injuries sustained in the accident and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 25-12-2018 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 06-10-2023, which is after lapse of four years and nine months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further he has stated that, out of the five fractures,
three fractures are united, one is malunited and joint dislocation is reduced.
Further, he has admitted that, there is no direct injury to the ankles.
Further, nowhere in the evidence the P.W.3 has stated that, the petitioner requires any further treatment for the said injuries.
Even, nothing with respect to, whether the petitioner has undergone complete treatment or not, is stated by the P.W.3.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after completion of treatment, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained by him, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was Proprietor of M/s. A.K.
Enterprises, carrying on the business of manufacturing and wholesale dealing in all kinds of school-college bags, traveling bags, fancy bags and complimentary bags and earning a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- to Rs.1,25,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do mason work.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.

He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was Proprietor of M/s. A.K. Enterprises and was doing the business of manufacturing and wholesale dealing in all kinds of school-college bags, traveling bags, fancy bags and complimentary bags and was earning Rs.1,00,000/- to Rs.1,25,000/- per month.

Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Ajaaj Ahmed vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89363345/

b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 60 years is 9.

ii) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred huge amount towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 28 medical bills, as per Ex.P.13.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.8,323/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.8,323/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.
suffered comminuted fracture of 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th metatarsal of left foot and medial cuneiform fracture 1 st metatarsal bones with dislocation of left foot, contusion injury left knee and contusion injury right ring finger.

As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary and Ex.P20 case-sheet, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 04 days from 26-12-2018 to 29- 12-2018, in V-care Hospital,
Bengaluru.
Further, as per P.W.3 the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore,
taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.20,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:

As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary and Ex.P20 case sheet, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 04 days from 26-12-2018 to 29- 12-2018, in V-care Hospital,
Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 4 = Rs.4,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:

As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary and Ex.P20 case sheet, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 04 days from 26-12- 2018 to 29-12-2018, in V-care Hospital,
Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 4 = Rs.3,200/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of R.T. Nagar, Bengaluru, the accident has taken place near Karnataka Spirit World, CBI Fly Over Under Pass, Service Road, Bengaluru and he has taken treatment at V- care Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between all the above three places, compensation of Rs.2,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 4 days as inpatient at V- care Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.

Therefore, Rs.12,500 x 2 =

viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 60 years and unfortunately he has suffered fracture of weight bearing bones i.e. comminuted fracture of 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th metatarsal of left foot and medial cuneiform fracture 1 st metatarsal bones with dislocation of left foot, contusion injury left knee and contusion injury right ring finger.
The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 8% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The petitioner has not produced any document to show that, he needs any further treatment for the injuries caused to him in the accident.
The P.W.3 has also not stated anything with regard to need of any further treatment to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

20. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 1,08,000-00 2.
Medical expenses 8,323-00 3. Pain and sufferings 20,000-00
4. Attendant charges 4,000-00 5.
Food and nourishment 3,200-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 2,000-00 7. Loss of income during 25,000-00 treatment period
8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses Nil Total Rs. 1,90,523-00
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,90,523/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
21. Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.
KA-50-V-8640 the accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.

However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,90,523/- from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,90,523/- (Rupees one lakh ninety thousand five hundred and twenty three only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This petition is filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was taken to M/s. V.
Care Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
Earlier to the accident, the petitioner was Proprietor of M/s. A.K. Enterprises and earning Rs.1,00,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident alleged to have occurred on 25-12-2018, at about 9:55 p.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motorcycle, bearing registration No.
KA-50-V-8640?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3. What order or Award?
6.
18. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 25-12-2018 at about 9.55 a.m., near Karnataka Spirit World, CBI Fly Over Under Pass, Service Road, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-50-V-8640.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The rider of offending motorcycle riding his motorcycle in wrong direction on a one way road itself proves his negligent driving.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.
When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle.
Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.7,
that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-50-V-8640.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the petitioner has sustained injuries due to his self rash and negligent driving and there is no negligence on the part of rider of offending motorcycle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, negligence of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can Ajaaj Ahmed vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89363345/
5 be safely held that, the respondent No.1 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-50-V-8640 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.
If the disability had been assessed after completion of treatment, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained by him, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was Proprietor of M/s. A.K. Enterprises and was doing the business of manufacturing and wholesale dealing in all kinds of school-college bags, traveling bags, fancy bags and complimentary bags and was earning Rs.1,00,000/- to Rs.1,25,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Ajaaj Ahmed vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89363345/
7 Services Authority.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.

Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.
20. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 1,08,000-00 2.

4. Attendant charges 4,000-00 5.

Conveyance expenses 2,000-00 7. Loss of income during 25,000-00 treatment period
8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses Nil Total Rs. 1,90,523-00
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,90,523/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,90,523/- from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,90,523/- (Rupees one lakh ninety thousand five hundred and twenty three only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
